description: Registry-level envelope validation and the catalog error codes it produces (invalid_envelope, unknown_command, invalid_field, unsupported). Malformed/closed-envelope cases are replayed verbatim through the raw_request-capable transports (direct, rest_generic, stdio); id echo/generation, unknown command and the options-unsupported cases use a real request envelope and run on every capability-eligible transport. Every code is asserted identically across transports.

cases.name: envelope_not_json
cases.doc: a body that is not JSON is rejected invalid_envelope with a server-minted id

cases.name: envelope_not_object
cases.doc: a top-level JSON array (not an object) is invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_missing_command
cases.doc: an envelope without the required command field is invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_bad_version
cases.doc: an unsupported envelope version (v=2) is invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_missing_version
cases.doc: an envelope without the required v field is invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_command_wrong_type
cases.doc: a non-string command (a number) is invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_id_too_long
cases.doc: a client id longer than the 64-byte cap is invalid_envelope; the response echoes a server-minted id, never the oversize client id

cases.name: envelope_extra_top_level_key
cases.doc: the closed envelope rejects an unknown top-level key with invalid_envelope

cases.name: envelope_options_non_boolean
cases.doc: a non-boolean options.dry_run is invalid_envelope (options carry only boolean dry_run/async)

cases.name: envelope_options_unknown_key
cases.doc: an unknown options key is invalid_envelope (the options object is closed)

cases.name: envelope_args_not_object
cases.doc: an args field that is a string, not an object, is invalid_envelope

cases.name: unknown_command_case_sensitive
cases.doc: an upper-case command name (LINK.CREATE) violates the lower-case command grammar and is rejected invalid_envelope at envelope validation, before registry lookup, identically on EVERY capability-eligible transport. Sent as a real request envelope (not raw_request) so the structured transports replay it too - in particular cli_cmd maps the invalid name to this same envelope instead of crashing with a FATAL line and exit 1 (see DEVIATIONS: spec table expected unknown_command, but the product rejects the malformed name shape first)

cases.name: envelope_nul_and_control_chars_in_string
cases.doc: a NUL (\u0000) inside a string arg is rejected invalid_field (not invalid_envelope: the envelope is well-formed, the decoded arg is not) and the process stays healthy - the following command.list still succeeds

cases.name: unknown_command_basic
cases.doc: a well-formed but unregistered command name is unknown_command (lookup fails after the envelope validates), identically on every transport

cases.name: envelope_id_echo
cases.doc: a request carrying an id has that id echoed in the response on every id-carrying transport (N4)

cases.name: envelope_id_generated
cases.doc: a request with no id gets a server-minted id (srv-<n>, or the cli-<n> the one-shot CLI mints); the harness checks the generated-id shape via N4

cases.name: options_unsupported_dry_run
cases.doc: options.dry_run on a command that does not support it (link.get) is unsupported, after authorization and arg validation pass (the slug is valid)

skip.rest_resource: rest_resource carries no envelope options block; the generic/CLI/stdio/TUI transports convey options and assert the unsupported outcome

cases.name: options_unsupported_async
cases.doc: options.async on a sync, non-async-capable command (link.create) is unsupported; valid args ensure the failure is the options mode, not validation

skip.rest_resource: rest_resource carries no envelope options block; the generic/CLI/stdio/TUI transports convey options and assert the unsupported outcome
